notes: Two halves, and the second is what makes the first mean anything: a stored status field could produce the same display and go stale silently. Pass/fail without judgement — the stage either changes or it does not, and the field either exists or it does not.
statement: With the application running, changing a recorded attestation so that a different stage becomes the earliest unready one causes the project view to display that stage as current, without restarting the application. No field storing a stage or status value exists anywhere under the content root.
title: The displayed current stage follows the attestations on disk

notes: ⚠️ NO PARTIAL-FAILURE EXCEPTION, deliberately. AST-0035 measured the skeleton printing 178 while rendering 177 — the count is what turns an incomplete page into a misleading one, because an operator reading the total has been told the missing thing is present. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-27, AND THE ORIGINAL WAS NOT MERELY IMPRECISE — IT WAS UNFALSIFIABLE. It asked that each displayed total equal 'the number rendered on the page'. The project view renders TOTALS, not artifact entries, so there is nothing on the page to count: the criterion compared a number with itself and would have passed on any implementation, including one that printed a constant. ⚠️ The fix is an INDEPENDENT ORACLE. A fixture with known composition is the only source of truth the application cannot influence, which is what makes this a test rather than a tautology. It is the same defect as a check nobody has seen fail (ACC-0024), reached from the other direction: there, the check had never been shown to fail; here, it could not.
statement: Evaluated against a fixture content root whose composition is known in advance. For each artifact type, the total the project view displays equals the number of files of that type in the fixture that parse successfully and validate. Ground truth comes from the fixture, not from the page: the count is computed independently of the application and compared with what was rendered.
title: Every displayed total equals the fixture's parsable artifacts of that type

notes: All three clauses are required together. Naming the file without correcting the count still leaves the page asserting an artifact it did not render; correcting the count without naming the file leaves an operator hunting for what changed.
statement: With exactly one artifact file under the content root made unparseable, the project view (a) names that file's path, (b) shows a parse position, and (c) prints a total for that type exactly one lower than before. The response is not an error page: every other artifact still renders.
title: An unreadable artifact is named, located, and subtracted from its count

notes: This is the clause that stops a page-level boundary satisfying DEC-0019 on paper. One boundary wrapping everything makes the whole page the fallback, which technically has a loading state and buys nothing.
statement: The initial HTML of the stage view contains a distinct loading fallback for the exit-criteria region and for the stage-document region. Delaying either read leaves the other region's content rendered and only its own fallback showing.
title: The stage view's reads resolve behind separate boundaries

notes: ⚠️ THE LAST SENTENCE IS THE WHOLE CRITERION. Stripping also produces a page with no executed code, so a test that renders a document and looks for a side effect passes identically on rejection and on silent removal — which is exactly the distinction the amendment to DEC-0020 exists to preserve. The observable being checked is the refusal, not the absence.
statement: For each of an ESM import, an ESM export, a flow expression, a text expression, a JSX attribute expression, a JSX spread attribute, and a JSX element outside the permitted set: compiling a stage document containing it produces a FAILURE that names the document path and a line:column position. A document that merely renders without the forbidden construct's effect is a FAIL for this criterion.
title: Each forbidden construct FAILS the compile with a file and position

notes: The negative criteria above are satisfiable by a compiler that refuses everything. This is the control that stops that.
statement: A stage document containing markdown and only components from the permitted set compiles, renders its markdown structure, and renders each permitted component it uses.
title: A permitted document renders, including its mapped components

notes: AST-0030 measured file-routed `@next/mdx` failing exactly this: the document is compiled into the build and an edit changes nothing. That configuration satisfies REQ-0017 and silently fails REQ-0018, which is why this is a criterion rather than an implementation note.
statement: With the built application serving, editing a stage document on disk changes what the next request for that stage returns, with no rebuild and no restart.
title: Stage documents compile at request time, not at build time

notes: ⚠️ THE 300 ms IS A TARGET, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and saying so is the point: DEC-0020 recorded this cost as explicitly unmeasured. If the first evaluation misses it by a wide margin the answer is not to relax the number — it is DEC-0020's own second alternative, plain markdown for stage documents. Recorded as a number rather than 'acceptable' so the criterion stays pass/fail. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-27 WITH A PROTOCOL, because the number alone was not a test. A budget with no pinned environment, no timing boundary and no warm-up treatment produces a figure nobody can reproduce or dispute, and 'p95 under 300 ms' would have been satisfiable by measuring the wrong thing on an unstated machine. ⚠️ THE VERIFICATION CLAUSE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST, and it is not routine hygiene. Without it the easiest way to pass is to cache the compiled document — which would report excellent numbers while measuring nothing, and would ALSO violate DEC-0020's request-time requirement and AST-0030's finding underneath it. A void run is not a failure and must not be recorded as one; it means the instrument was wrong, which is a different problem from the budget being missed. ⚠️ The 300 ms is still a TARGET rather than a measurement, and DEC-0020's third obligation stands: if the first valid run misses it by a wide margin the answer is that decision's own second alternative, plain markdown for stage documents — not a larger number. ⚠️ EVALUATED 2026-08-28 (EVD-0071): FAIL, and the reason is not the compiler. Six valid runs, three at 245-254 ms and three at 315-375 ms against the 300 ms budget. A criterion stated as a p95 ceiling is not met when half the valid measurements are above it, so this is `fail` rather than a pass with a caveat — but it is also NOT the failure this criterion anticipated. ⚠️ THE FALLBACK CLAUSE IS AIMED AT THE WRONG COST. MDX compilation measured 15-29 ms p95, 4-12% of the span; the planning-content read measured 234-359 ms. Applying DEC-0020's second alternative would surrender the restricted-MDX contract to remove roughly 20 ms and would still miss the budget. That clause was written when the cost was unmeasured; it now is, and it is somewhere else. ⚠️ THE PROTOCOL ITSELF NEEDS ONE MORE PIN. It fixes the host, document, warm-up, sample and timing boundary, but 'no other significant load' is not enforceable, and the read is I/O and validation heavy enough that ambient load moves the p95 by 50%. A protocol whose verdict flips between identical runs cannot settle a pass/fail question, whatever the number is. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-28: the 234-359 ms span was attributed here to reading all 253 artifacts per request. It is not. `readStageDocument` awaits `connection()` and reads the nine stage documents only — `lintProject` is not on its path. What inside that span costs the time is an open question, not a known cost. ⚠️ SUPERSEDED 2026-08-28 BY ACC-0037, WITH THE FAILURE LEFT STANDING. The outcome remains `fail` and this record remains readable: the budget was missed and that is history now, not a tick that was quietly flipped. What changed is the question being asked. This criterion bounded read-plus-compile, and the measurement showed the read dominates and the compiler does not, so ACC-0037 bounds the compile alone and QST-0025 carries the read as an open question. DEC-0025 records why the plain-Markdown fallback did not fire. ⚠️ THE SUCCESSOR IS NOT THIS ONE RELABELLED. Superseding a failed criterion with a wider version of the same claim would be editing the failure rather than answering it; the successor measures a different, narrower thing, and the part it dropped is carried by a question rather than dropped.
statement: The 95th-percentile server-side time to compile and render the largest stage document in the project is at or below 300 ms, measured under this protocol. ENVIRONMENT: the reference host, with its OS, Node version, Next.js version and CPU model recorded alongside the result; no other significant load. DOCUMENT: the largest stage document by byte count at the time of evaluation, named in the result. TIMING BOUNDARY: from the moment the request handler begins the planning-content read to the moment the rendered document markup is complete, measured server-side; network and client time are excluded. WARM-UP: 10 requests are issued and discarded before measurement begins. SAMPLE: the next 50 consecutive requests, issued one at a time with no concurrency, are the measured set. VERIFICATION: each of the 50 must be shown to have actually compiled — a counter incremented per compile, or an equivalent observation, reported with the result. A run in which any measured request did not compile is VOID, not a pass.
title: Per-request compilation stays within 300 ms at p95, under a pinned protocol

notes: ⚠️ 'Without executing the application' is load-bearing. AST-0022 measured that a non-compliant read is served FRESH whenever a compliant read shares its route, so every behavioural check passes on a codebase that violates the contract until the compliant sibling moves.
statement: A check that runs WITHOUT executing the application reports a failure naming file and line when any module other than the planning-content reader performs a filesystem read rooted at the content directory.
title: The boundary check fails on a planning-content read outside the reader

notes: The clause that gets dropped. An abstraction can supply `connection()` while a caller omits the boundary; that builds fine without Cache Components and fails the build with it, so the omission would surface as an unrelated configuration change breaking the build.
statement: The same non-executing check reports a failure when a planning-content read site is not enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary, naming file and line.
title: The boundary check fails on a read outside a Suspense boundary

notes: The indirect clause is the bypass path DEC-0021 requires be detected. A direct import is easy to find; a module that re-exports `lib/` and is then imported freely is the same violation wearing one layer.
statement: The same non-executing check reports a failure naming file and line when any module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`, including through a re-export chain that reaches `lib/` indirectly.
title: The boundary check fails on an app module importing `lib/` directly

notes: ⚠️ ADDED BECAUSE IT HAPPENED. A refusal test written during this work passed with the refusal deleted — the assertion that mattered sat behind a condition that was never true. A check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody has seen. This criterion is what makes the three above mean something rather than merely exist.
statement: The check is evaluated against a fixture set containing at least one instance of each violation it claims to detect, and reports a failure for every one. A check that passes the fixture set is a FAIL for this criterion.
title: The boundary check is itself falsified against known violations

statement: Every module under `app/server/` has `import 'server-only'` as its first statement and contains no `export *`. Checked statically over the whole directory, with no exemptions.
title: Every adapter module is guarded and explicitly exported

notes: AST-0033 measured `server-only` throwing outside the RSC compiler. This criterion is what stops the guard migrating into `lib/` later as a tidy-up and breaking the tool to protect the app.
statement: Every command under `bin/` and the full test suite run to completion with the shell present, importing `lib/` directly under plain Node with no RSC compiler in play.
title: `lib/` stays importable under plain Node

notes: ⚠️ THE WORDING CLAUSE IS MEASURED, NOT STYLISTIC. Next.js produced two different messages for the same violation reached two ways, and one of them said 'you are using it in the Pages Router' for an App Router project. A test pinned to that string would pass on a wrong message today and break on a corrected one after an upgrade.
statement: A `'use client'` module importing any `app/server/` adapter causes the build to fail with a message naming the offending file and a line:column position. The criterion asserts the presence of a file and a position, and MUST NOT assert the diagnostic's wording.
title: A client component reaching an adapter fails the build, locatably

notes: ⚠️ AST-0036: a line beginning with a colon is ignored by the client parser, so a comment heartbeat keeps the socket warm and fires nothing. The criterion is the listener firing, not bytes arriving, because bytes arriving was never the problem.
statement: While connected and with no content changing, the stream delivers an event with a name and a data field at least once per configured heartbeat interval, and a client listener registered for that event name fires. A comment-only keepalive is a FAIL for this criterion.
title: The stream emits a named heartbeat event that page code can observe

notes: AST-0034 measured the skeleton's idle and dead streams as byte-identical, which is the strongest possible form of indistinguishable. 'Not by colour alone' keeps the fix legible to anyone who cannot rely on a colour difference.
statement: When heartbeats stop arriving, the page shows a stale indication that is distinguishable from the healthy state by text or icon and not by colour alone, within the configured watchdog window.
title: A stopped heartbeat produces a visibly stale page within the watchdog window

notes: AST-0034 measured the gap being lost with nothing to recover it from. The last sentence records the design that makes this cheap: because events are hints and never deltas, a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up.
statement: After the stream drops and reconnects, the client reloads, and a content change made during the disconnected window is reflected in what the page then shows. No event buffer, event id or `Last-Event-ID` handling is required to achieve this.
title: Reconnection reloads, and a change made while disconnected is then visible

notes: The operator is looking at a browser, not a terminal. A logged failure with a live-looking page is the retained-workspace-reported-destroyed defect in its purest form: the system knows, records it accurately, and tells the person who needs it nothing.
statement: When the file watcher fails, the page shows the stale indication or the stream closes. A run in which the failure appears only in server output while the page continues to indicate health is a FAIL.
title: A watcher failure reaches the page, never only a log

notes: 'Verified by observation, not by the absence of an error' is the tier-1 controller's own rule arriving here: a removal that reports success while the directory survives is retained, and the check has to be `exists()` rather than `!threw`. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: THERE IS NO SECOND PROCESS, AND THERE NEVER WAS ONE TO OWN. This artifact previously said the launcher owns 'both the application process and the file watcher' and 'terminates the watcher with the application'. The watcher is chokidar, imported dynamically INSIDE the `next start` process and held by the change-stream service in that process's memory. A parent launcher cannot call `changeStream.close()` across that boundary without adding IPC or a shutdown endpoint, and neither is justified for a local-first tool. The old wording described a mechanism that could not be built, which is worse than an unmet obligation: it would have been 'satisfied' by a launcher that called nothing and reported success. ⚠️ WHAT IS TRUE INSTEAD, and all of it is enforceable. The launcher owns ONE child: the `next start` process. The change-stream service owns its watcher and closes it when its last subscriber leaves — already built and tested under TSK-0011. Terminating the application process releases any watcher still open through process teardown, which is the operating system's guarantee rather than the launcher's. `close()` stays what it is: a service and test lifecycle operation, never something the launcher claims to call across a process boundary. ⚠️ THIS CRITERION WAS UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AMENDED RATHER THAN REPHRASED. It required that 'no watcher process remains'. There is no watcher process, so the clause could never be observed either true or false — and an unobservable clause in a criterion whose whole point is 'verified by observation, not by the absence of an error' is the exact defect that rule exists to catch, sitting inside the rule. It is amended rather than superseded because it has never been evaluated: no measurement is being retired, and there is no failed outcome to preserve. ⚠️ THE HEARTBEAT PRECONDITION IS PART OF THE CRITERION, not of the test that runs it. The watcher is created lazily on first subscription, so a run that never subscribed would satisfy every remaining clause while having nothing to clean up.
statement: After the documented launch command is run and then terminated, the child process it started is gone, no process is listening on the application's port, and no temporary directory the launcher created survives — each verified by observation, not by the absence of an error. The run must have opened `/events` and observed a heartbeat before termination, so that a file watcher is known to have existed.
title: Stopping the launcher leaves nothing behind

notes: 'No further steps' is the testable half. DEC-0018 fixes the mode: `next build` then `next start`, never the development server. ⚠️ MARKED `pass` IN ERROR ON 2026-08-29 AND RETURNED TO `not-evaluated` THE SAME DAY. EVD-0073 recorded, in its own omissions, that the install branch was never taken: `node_modules` was present in every run, so the launcher printed `dependencies present; skipping install`. This criterion says 'on a machine with... no prior application state' and 'installs and starts'. Half of it was measured and the whole of it was ticked. ⚠️ THE EVIDENCE ITSELF SAID SO, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. The omission was written down accurately and then contradicted by the outcome three lines later — a criterion marked against evidence that explicitly disclaims the thing being claimed. Recording an omission is not the same as honouring it. ⚠️ WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the documented command run in a disposable copy of the repository with no `node_modules` and no `.next`, installing, building, serving and cleaning up with no further steps. ⚠️ EVALUATED PROPERLY 2026-08-29 (EVD-0074) AND RETURNED TO `pass`. The documented command was run in a disposable copy holding only tracked files, with `node_modules` and `.next` confirmed absent. It installed, built, served and cleaned up in 27.2s with no further steps, and the install branch was asserted positively rather than inferred from the run succeeding.
statement: On a machine with the repository and Node present and no prior application state, the documented command installs and starts the application in production mode, and the project view responds, without further steps. The install is conditional and the command says which branch it took: a cold checkout installs; a warm checkout whose root lockfile is not newer than npm's installed-tree marker skips the install; and a missing or stale marker installs rather than guessing about a tree npm did not lay down. ⚠️ THE FRESHNESS COMPARISON IS AGAINST npm's MARKER, NOT THE `node_modules` DIRECTORY mtime. A directory's mtime moves only when an entry is added or removed at its top level, which reinstalling the same tree does not do, while `npm install` touches the lockfile every time — so comparing the two made the condition permanently true and the documented command reinstalled on every start, which is the outcome a conditional install exists to prevent.
title: The application installs and starts from one documented command

notes: The byte-identical clause is what makes this objective rather than a claim about intent. #82's two-axis split is the reason `lifecycle` is named explicitly: one `status` field would have let this endpoint retire an artifact by accident.
statement: The review action identifies the artifact by id and type and shows its current status. Submitting a change updates only that artifact's `reviewStatus`, through the existing typed write path with its lock and atomic write; the artifact's `lifecycle` and every other artifact on disk are byte-identical afterwards.
title: A review update changes one artifact's reviewStatus and nothing else

notes: ⚠️ SCOPED TO CORRECTNESS-CRITICAL STATE, per DEC-0023's corrected wording. Transient interface state is permitted and is not covered here. The reason this needs a criterion at all is that DEC-0022 reloads the page on every content change and every reconnection — at a moment the user did not choose, and without telling them what was lost.
statement: For each selection the views expose that is not purely presentational — at minimum the selected stage and the selected artifact — opening the same URL in a session with no prior client storage restores the same selection.
title: Every correctness-critical selection survives a reload in a fresh session

notes: ⚠️ WRITTEN FROM A MEASUREMENT, not from caution. AST-0039 recorded what production actually does when the compiler refuses a document inside a `<Suspense>` boundary: HTTP 200, because the shell has already streamed, and a React error digest with no message, no path and no position. The compiler's diagnostic is exact and reaches only the server log. ⚠️ 200 IS NOT THE DEFECT AND IS EXPLICITLY ACCEPTED. Streaming means the status is committed before the failure is known, and demanding a 5xx would mean giving up streaming for a document the operator can be told about in place. What is refused is INVISIBILITY — a blank region and a success status for a document the compiler rejected precisely. ⚠️ THE ESCAPING CLAUSE IS NOT HOUSEKEEPING. The diagnostic quotes the offending source, which is agent-authored content; rendering it as markup would let a refused document inject into the page that reports its refusal — turning the safety mechanism into the delivery route. ⚠️ 'The rest of the page still renders' is what makes this a criterion about ONE region rather than about error handling in general: the exit criteria live behind their own boundary and a refused document must not take them down with it.
statement: When the restricted compiler refuses a stage document, the served page renders an error inside the document region that (a) is visible in the response body, (b) names the document by a REPOSITORY-RELATIVE path, (c) carries a line and column, and (d) has its diagnostic text HTML-escaped rather than interpolated as markup. The stage's exit criteria and the rest of the page still render. A partial page returning HTTP 200 satisfies this criterion; a response whose document region contains only an opaque error digest, or nothing at all, FAILS it.
title: A refused stage document fails VISIBLY, in the document region, with a location

notes: ⚠️ IT SUCCEEDS ACC-0020 AND IT IS NOT ACC-0020 WITH A BIGGER NUMBER. The predecessor bounded read-plus-compile at 300 ms and failed, but the measurement showed the failure came from the read. Widening that budget would have hidden a real unknown behind a comfortable ceiling. This one bounds only the cost that was ever in dispute — whether request-time MDX compilation is affordable — and the read it excluded is carried by its own open question, not dropped. ⚠️ 50 ms IS ROUGHLY TWICE THE MEASURED WORST CASE (29.05 ms p95 across six runs), chosen as headroom for document growth rather than as a description of today. A criterion set at the measurement passes by construction and detects nothing. ⚠️ THE VERIFICATION CLAUSE IS INHERITED DELIBERATELY, and it has been falsified: memoising the compiled document makes `bin/bench-compile.mjs` report VOID with a non-zero exit and no timing figures at all. Without it the cheapest way to pass a compile budget is to stop compiling, which would also break DEC-0020's request-time requirement and AST-0030's finding beneath it. ⚠️ EVALUATED `pass` ON EVD-0071, the same six runs that failed the predecessor: compile p95 was 15.41-29.05 ms in every one. The evidence did not change; the question it was asked did.
statement: The 95th-percentile time spent in `compileStageDocument` for the largest stage document is at or below 50 ms. MEASURED SPAN: the compile call alone — from the moment the reader's document is handed to the compiler to the moment a renderable component is returned — EXCLUDING the planning-content read that precedes it, which is a separate cost under a separate question. ENVIRONMENT: the reference host, with its OS, Node version, Next.js version, @mdx-js/mdx version and CPU model recorded alongside the result; no other significant load. DOCUMENT: the largest stage document by byte count at the time of evaluation, named in the result. WARM-UP: 10 requests issued and discarded. SAMPLE: the next 50 consecutive requests, issued one at a time with no concurrency. VERIFICATION: the compile counter must advance by exactly one per measured request. A run in which any measured request did not compile is VOID, not a pass.
title: Restricted-MDX compilation stays within 50 ms at p95, under ACC-0020's protocol

notes: PASS 2026-09-03. Mechanised in test/pi-compat.test.mjs inside `assertContract()`, which is applied to the retained record AND to the live run: trust rows 4 and 5 revert the grant, the sentinel control shows secrets crossing under inheritance, the prose and exclusion controls show no tool executing, the override-removal control restores the packaged skill, the no-credential control leaves the model unavailable, the without-variable control leaves the env-authenticated model unavailable while an inline-key provider is listed in both, and the default-directory control shows the override actually moved something. ⚠️ TWO GAPS WERE FOUND IN THIS CRITERION'S OWN ENFORCEMENT AND BOTH ARE CLOSED. The packaged prompt proof had only a successful expansion: `literalSlashStringReachedProvider: false` in the SAME run is the other half of one observation, not a control, and would read identically if the template had expanded for a reason unrelated to package loading. There is now a separate run with trust revoked in which the package does not load, the body marker does not arrive, and the literal slash string survives. ⚠️ AND `reachedObservationPoint()` ACCEPTED ANY TERMINATED PROCESS THAT EMITTED ANY OUTPUT — so a CLI dying on a bad argument would have had its missing marker read as a trust result. It now requires a `session` event in the transcript, which is emitted after the point where the load-time marker would have been written. An absent marker beside a session event is a real negative; an absent marker beside no session event is a void run, and the test refuses it.
statement: For each behaviour the compatibility suite establishes, the recorded evidence contains both the observation and a control run in which the claimed behaviour is absent and the observation does not appear. A claim recorded with only a positive run fails this criterion, and so does a negative result whose transcript does not show the process reaching the point where the observation would have been made.
title: Every spike claim carries a negative control that would have failed

notes: PASS 2026-09-03. Retained results exist for both platforms and each names its platform, Node version and the pinned Pi version. ⚠️ THE TEST ALSO FAILS ON A PIN BUMP: it compares the pin in package.json against the pin the evidence was taken under and refuses a mismatch, naming the command to re-run. That is what stops a version change inheriting the previous version's evidence. POSIX was measured on Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2 and the live tier re-runs on ubuntu-latest in CI. ⚠️ 'RECORDS WHICH PLATFORM' NOW MEANS SOMETHING TO THE DERIVATION ENGINE, which it did not before: the environment facts were written as prose — `platform: 'windows and linux'`, `piVersion: '0.84.4, installed by...'` — and the engine compares facts by exact equality, so every supporting record was excluded and ten of twelve spike assertions derived as unverified while reading as proved. Facts are scalars now, prose lives in summaries, and the one observation whose RESULT differs by platform has a single-platform record of its own.
statement: Each recorded observation names the platform, the exact pinned Pi version, and the Node version it was taken on, and the suite has been executed to completion on both Windows and the project's supported POSIX CI platform. A behaviour observed on one platform only is recorded as single-platform rather than as the contract.
title: The suite runs on Windows and on the supported POSIX platform and records which

notes: PASS 2026-09-03, AND IT FAILED THREE TIMES FIRST — the sequence is the point. (1) The initial result set was saved unredacted and was full of absolute home paths. (2) The second version redacted the summary while npm's output went straight to the terminal and was captured nowhere, so the test scanned a summary while the criterion said 'command output'. (3) The third still omitted `pi install -l`, the fake provider's streams, and every generated file, and the DETECTOR could not see a Windows home path once JSON-escaped — `C:\\Users\\alice` in serialised bytes returned an empty violation list while the raw string was flagged. ⚠️ NARROWED TO WHAT IS ACTUALLY COVERED, AND THE COVERAGE WIDENED TO MEET IT. The scope is now RETAINED bytes, enumerated; streamed-and-discarded output is explicitly out, because a criterion nothing can check is worse than a narrower one. ⚠️ THE DETECTOR AND THE REDACTOR ARE TESTED AGAINST EACH OTHER, in both directions: every forbidden shape must be SEEN by the detector before the redactor is asked to remove it, and both must handle the JSON-escaped form. They disagreed twice — once with the redactor weaker, once with the detector weaker — and the second is the dangerous direction.
statement: Every byte the suite RETAINS is asserted to contain no API key, OAuth token, authorisation header, credential-derived fingerprint, username, or absolute user-home path. What is retained is enumerated and complete: the result summary; the captured stdout and stderr of every subprocess the suite starts, including the consumer's `npm install`, `pi install -l`, every Pi child, the model-registry probes and the fake provider; and the generated state the suite produced — the provider request log, the project settings file and the trust store. The assertion runs over those captured bytes rather than over a summary of them; redaction happens at write time and the runner refuses to save a file that still violates the rule. Output that is streamed and discarded is out of scope, because nothing can scan it.
title: No spike artefact contains credential material

statement: With a different Pi version installed globally and earlier on PATH, every Pi process Kiln starts reports the pinned version. A test that removes the local dependency causes a refusal naming the expected version and the resolved path, rather than falling through to the global binary.
title: Pi is resolved from the tool's node_modules and never from PATH

notes: PASS 2026-09-03, mechanised in `test/content-root.test.mjs`. ⚠️ THE TESTS ARE WRITTEN AROUND THE DIVERGENCE, NOT THE AGREEMENT. `dirname(contentRoot)` and `<toolRoot>/..` name the same directory in an ordinary consumer install, so a resolver that took the wrong one would pass every test that did not set the override. The override case therefore asserts BOTH that the answer is the owner of the overridden directory AND that it is not the tool's parent — which is a real directory and a plausible wrong answer. ⚠️ CANONICAL COMPARISON IS PART OF THE CRITERION because without it the refusal misfires: a correct setup invocation arriving by a symlinked path would read as a disagreement, and a refusal that fires on correct input is worse than none. Covered with a junction, skipped rather than failed where symlink creation is privileged. ⚠️ SCOPE: THIS IS THE RESOLVER, AND ONLY THE RESOLVER. The obligation that SETUP calls it — printing every canonicalised path before the first lasting write, and refusing on disagreement — is ACC-0085 against CMP-0039, and is correctly still not-evaluated because setup does not exist. The third clause here previously read as though it were about setup; it is about the thing that does the refusing, which is what can be evaluated now.
statement: With PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR unset, the resolved project root is the parent of the content root derived from the tool location; with it set, it is the canonical parent of that explicit directory and NOT the tool's parent, asserted as a distinct value rather than merely as the right one. Given an explicit project root that disagrees with the resolved content owner, the resolver refuses and its message names both paths, the rule that produced the resolved one, and the override — rather than choosing between them. Comparison is canonical, so two spellings of one directory do not read as a disagreement.
title: The project root is derived from the resolved content root, and a mismatch refuses

statement: Running setup twice with the same inputs against the same project leaves every file it owns byte-identical, including the settings file, the ignore block, the project identity file and the generated skills. The comparison is over file bytes, not over a reported status.
title: A rerun with unchanged choices changes no bytes

statement: When a file the transaction recorded is modified after the plan is built and before the merge runs, the transaction detects the changed identity under the lock and refuses, leaving the operator's edit intact. A malformed or unknown-schema-version file likewise refuses rather than being replaced.
title: A file edited between plan and merge refuses rather than overwriting

statement: Killing setup partway through leaves a journal naming the last completed phase and an exact resume command; running that command completes the remaining phases. A failure in any agent phase leaves an already-initialised planning scaffold in place and reports partial setup rather than rolling it back.
title: An interrupted setup resumes from its journal and never deletes valid content

statement: A fresh project receives exactly one Kiln-marked block containing `.planning/`, `.pi/sessions/` and `.pi/runtime/`. An exact unmodified legacy block containing only `.planning/` is migrated to the extended block with every byte outside the markers preserved, and the migration is recorded and byte-stable on rerun. A block the operator removed or edited is reported and requires an explicit choice; it is never silently rewritten.
title: One owner writes the ignore block, and a removed block is not restored

statement: A settings file carrying third-party packages, unrelated keys and a custom key order is merged with Kiln's four owned fields and every unrelated entry is preserved and not reordered gratuitously. A malformed file, or one declaring an unknown schema version, is refused with the file left unchanged.
title: Unrelated settings and package entries survive the merge untouched

statement: After a complete setup against an environment-authenticated provider and an enabled research connection, the committed `.pi/settings.json` and `.pi/kiln.json` are asserted to contain no API key, token, authorisation header, credential-derived fingerprint, or absolute user path.
title: The committed settings file contains no secret and no absolute home path

statement: With the Kiln ignore block absent or edited, project-local mode writes no session, consent, compatibility or journal file: interactive setup offers the exact block, external state, or stopping, and non-interactive setup refuses. The check is that the paths do not exist after the refusal, not that a warning was printed.
title: No runtime data is written before its protection exists

statement: In external mode the state root derives from the platform convention and the committed non-secret project ID; two projects on one machine occupy separate roots; and no committed file contains an absolute user path. The mode is available only if the pinned runtime supports relocation.
title: External state derives from the committed project ID with no path committed

statement: Interactive setup displays the canonical project path and obtains the decision through Pi's own supported mechanism. A denial leaves the planning scaffold intact and valid, does not describe the agent as ready, and still permits an explicit browser-only start. Non-interactive setup with no pre-existing decision refuses rather than defaulting to approval.
title: Trust is obtained through a supported route, and a denial stops the agent cleanly

statement: Before the inspection prompt is answered, no read of Pi's authentication store, no load of the custom-model registry and no credential-variable presence check has occurred — observed by instrumenting those access points, not by reading the code. A declined inspection performs none of them, contacts nothing, and leaves setup honestly partial rather than reporting that nothing is configured.
title: Nothing is read before permission, and a decline reads nothing at all

statement: The presented result contains provider display names, exact model identifiers and present-or-absent for the research credential, and is asserted to contain no key, token, header, environment value or credential-derived fingerprint. No external service is contacted during the inspection.
title: Inspection results report availability and never credential material

statement: A project carrying a committed research choice, opened on a machine with no local consent record, reopens the prompt and does not use that host's credential until it is answered. Changing the provider or the research choice likewise reopens the relevant prompt.
title: A clone does not inherit the first operator's consent

statement: When discovery returns exactly one usable model, setup displays its provider display name and exact identifier and requires confirmation before assigning it. Pi's global default and the first entry in discovery order are never adopted implicitly, and a mutable alias is never selected on the operator's behalf.
title: A single available model still requires confirmation, and no default is adopted

statement: With the recorded model removed from the registry, or its authentication absent, launch refuses and names the recorded provider and model, offering a setup rerun or an explicit one-run override. No other model, provider, or answer from model memory is substituted.
title: An unavailable recorded selection refuses instead of falling back

notes: ⚠️ THE CONTROL IS PART OF THE CRITERION, not a nicety. A sentinel test with no control passes identically whether the boundary works or the sentinels were never set. ⚠️ IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN AS 'the child sees only the union', which was the first phrasing and is not achievable: Windows injects nine home and user variables into every child regardless of the environment supplied (AST-0045). What is provable on both platforms is that no secret Kiln did not choose to pass is among what the child receives.
statement: With unrelated secrets present in the parent environment under names a naive implementation would match, a spawned specialist child's observed environment contains none of them, while a control child spawned with the environment inherited observes all of them. Kiln adds to the child only the measured base variables, the selected provider's declared model-plane names and that role's tool-plane names. The assertion is made over what the child observed, not over what the parent intended.
title: A sentinel host secret never reaches a child, against a control that shows one crossing

statement: A provider whose credential contract is neither built in nor declared through the validated custom shape yields an `unsupported-credential-contract` refusal naming the provider. No additional variables are inherited, and no variable name is inferred from the provider id or discovered by scanning the environment.
title: An unknown environment-only provider is refused, not widened

statement: The research child receives the research credential when research is enabled and not otherwise; planning and validation children never receive it in any configuration.
title: Research holds the only tool-plane credential, and only while enabled

statement: The prompt names the exact provider and model and states that the provider may charge. Declining leaves a valid content and browser setup, does not mark the agent ready, does not begin intake, and is reported as a choice rather than a failure. Non-interactive runs require an explicit approval flag when no matching record exists.
title: The canary is separately approved, names the cost, and declining is not an error

statement: The canary passes only when the model invokes the setup-only tool with the exact random challenge against the declared schema, observed through the real pinned runtime and provider path. A response that merely claims tool support, or that calls the tool with a malformed argument, fails.
title: Success requires an observed tool call with the right challenge and schema

statement: During the canary no planning content is sent and no mutation tool is reachable; the setup-only tool is absent from the user-facing orchestrator and from every specialist. The stored success record contains no credential or credential-derived value, and changing the provider, model, thinking level, runtime version, package capability signature or endpoint identity invalidates it and reopens approval.
title: The canary cannot see or change planning content, and its record invalidates correctly

statement: With the project trusted, a real Pi run loads the package's extensions, tools, skills and start prompt and exposes a capability signature. With trust absent the package does not load — and that state is detected and reported rather than passing silently, which is the control that makes the positive result meaningful.
title: The package loads under trust, does not load without it, and reports its signature

statement: The user-facing session's measured active tool set contains the registered Kiln tools and does not contain Pi's built-in shell, write or edit tools. The measurement is of the session's reported registry, not of what the launch options requested.
title: The orchestrator holds Kiln's typed tools and none of Pi's built-in mutation tools

statement: Each registered mutation tool writes through the existing locked, atomic, validated path with the content root resolved by the shared resolver, returns structured success or refusal, and leaks no credential or absolute home path in its result. Business rules stay in `lib/`; the wrapper adds schema and rendering only.
title: Every wrapper resolves the canonical content root and preserves the write discipline

statement: Each packaged stage skill carries the purpose, outputs and exit criteria of its canonical definition, produced by a generator rather than hand-maintained. Editing a stage definition without regenerating makes the check mode fail in CI, naming the stale skill.
title: Packaged skills are generated, and staleness fails a check

statement: With the consumer's override directory registered after the packaged set, a real Pi resource load resolves the override file for a skill of the same identity; editing the override changes what loads; removing it reverts to the packaged skill. Provenance is read from the loaded file path, not from model behaviour.
title: An override with the same identity wins, and removing it reverts

statement: On a fresh project the orchestrator reads the name, description and starter document and responds with a single relevant question. It proposes no architecture, no requirement set and no solution, and the answer it receives is written into the intake document through the typed path rather than by editing the file.
title: The first Stage 1 turn asks one question and invents no solution

statement: After the intake document changes, the next question differs according to what the answer supplied — demonstrated by driving two different first answers from the same starting state and observing two different second questions.
title: The second question is chosen from updated state, not from a list

statement: An attempt to advance or attest Stage 1 without explicit operator authorisation is refused by the orchestrator, and no attestation file changes. The refusal is observable in the recorded state, not only in the transcript.
title: The orchestrator cannot cross a user-owned gate

statement: Started in a consumer checkout, the orchestrator resolves the canonical sibling content root; given a state in which the tool's own bundled content would resolve instead, it refuses and names both paths rather than authoring into the tool's plan.
title: It refuses to operate on the tool's own planning content

statement: A real Pi run of each specialist reports an active tool set equal to the intersection of that role's declared allowlist and the measured host registry. A role definition with no declared tool list fails the roster lint rather than inheriting Pi's default active set.
title: Each role has exactly its contract's tools, and a missing allowlist is a lint error

statement: No shipped role definition contains a model declaration, and a specialist run reports the same provider, model and thinking level as the orchestrator that delegated to it.
title: No role declares a model

statement: One test asserts both facts about the same child: its stdin was closed, and the exact delegated task reached it through the supported non-stdin channel, observed at the child. The verifier's field and its refusal reason describe task binding rather than stdin.
title: Stdin is closed and the exact task still arrived

statement: A child that exits zero, emits a well-formed transcript and returns plausible prose without Kiln's tools causes the delegation to fail loudly; none of its substantive output is used. The same holds for signature drift, an out-of-role write, a nonzero exit, a timeout, malformed JSON events, a missing task binding and a provider or model mismatch.
title: A child without the Kiln capability signature is refused, not read

statement: The child's reported provider, model and thinking level equal the orchestrator's, it receives a task-scoped payload rather than the conversation, and temporary prompt material is absent from disk after every exit path including timeout and abort.
title: The child inherits the orchestrator's exact selection and a scoped context

statement: The endpoint returns exactly the keys service, protocol, runId, projectId and build — no more and no fewer, as a set rather than in a fixed order — with the service name and the versioned protocol fixed, the run and project identifiers equal to the ones supplied to this process, and the build version read from the package the running code was loaded from rather than from the environment, which could only ever match itself. A response carrying an additional key, missing a key, or carrying the two identifiers exchanged, fails; asserting only the absence of known sensitive patterns does not satisfy this, because it passes on every field nobody thought to pattern-match. Every field of a successful response is built from a validated value: both identifiers must be strings matching the fixed 32-character lowercase hexadecimal format, and the build version must match a character set containing no path separator, colon or whitespace. Nothing that fails those checks is echoed, so the absence of any absolute path, credential, session content or planning content holds by construction across the whole response rather than by scanning the output. An identity that is not whole is not an identity: a missing, unreadable or unsafe build version answers 503 exactly as a missing run identity does, never a 200 with a null field. Each failure answers with its own exact key set and a distinguishing error, never a 200 with fields missing and never an invented identifier. The status, headers and parsed body are observed over real HTTP for both the identified and the unidentified case, and the served identity is proved to come from the running process rather than the build by starting the application with an identity different from the one present when it was built.
title: The health response is exactly an identity, asserted field by field

statement: Two proofs are required together, because either alone passes in the arrangement this criterion forbids. Structurally: under the supervisor the application launcher is spawned with a private stdin the supervisor can WRITE to and CLOSE, while Pi is spawned with the terminal inherited. Behaviourally: with a launcher-side reader actively attempting to consume input, an exact sentinel written to the supervisor's own stdin is received by Pi and the launcher-side reader receives none of that sentinel — it is expected to receive the supervisor's later stop control message, which is its own channel working. A positive check that input reached Pi does not satisfy this on its own: it passes whenever Pi happens to win a read, including when both processes hold the terminal, which is precisely the defect. The control must fail when the launcher's stdin is changed from a private pipe to inherited terminal input, and a control that survives that mutation has not tested this criterion. The launcher continues to stop on the stop control message and on its stdin being closed. ⚠️ SCOPE OF THE EVIDENCE: the harness supplies a pipe rather than a pseudo-terminal, so what is proved is descriptor ownership and byte routing, not terminal line discipline or signal behaviour. The structural assertion is what ties it to the real topology — whatever descriptor 0 is, the launcher is not given it.
title: The background launcher cannot read the terminal, proved against an adversary

statement: With an unrelated server already answering on the chosen port, launch refuses rather than reporting the browser ready. A response carrying a wrong run identifier, a wrong project identifier, or arriving while the expected child is not alive, likewise fails readiness.
title: An unrelated healthy HTTP service does not satisfy readiness

statement: A port outside 1..65535 or a non-integer value is refused. When the default is occupied, interactive mode offers another available port for that invocation only and non-interactive mode refuses with an exact PORT recovery command. An automatically chosen port is never written into project configuration.
title: Port handling refuses out-of-range values and never silently persists a choice

statement: After Pi exits, or after an interrupt, both process trees are stopped within their grace periods, the port is free, and only files created by that invocation were removed. Verified on Windows and on the supported POSIX platform.
title: Shutdown leaves nothing running on either platform

statement: Run where the tool root and project root are the same directory, the normal command refuses rather than writing `.pi/` into the tool repository. The opt-in requires both the explicit content-directory override and the self-host flag, and the supervisor verifies the two agree before starting.
title: The self-hosting checkout is refused unless explicitly opted into

statement: A static check of the setup command's import graph, up to and including the dependency-install step, finds no import of any installed dependency. Adding a top-level import of the Pi runtime or the validator makes that check fail.
title: The pre-install import graph uses Node built-ins only

statement: Invalid arguments, content conflict, filesystem or settings refusal, missing runtime, trust denial, interactive authentication required, provider or credential-contract failure, live compatibility refusal, package or capability failure, and launch failure each exit with their own code, and the mapping in `--help` matches the codes the tests observe.
title: Each refusal class has a distinct published exit code

statement: Before the first lasting write, the command has printed the canonicalised tool root, project root, content root, settings path and runtime state path. A disagreement between the explicit project root and the resolved content owner refuses and prints both.
title: Setup prints every path before it mutates anything

statement: From a temporary empty directory the documented sequence — including `git init` into a repository with no commits, before any commit exists — initialises, installs, registers, binds a deterministic non-billable model, starts both processes with identity-confirmed readiness, and reaches a Stage 1 question. Verified on Windows and the supported POSIX CI platform.
title: The documented journey completes from an empty directory on both platforms

statement: A deterministic Stage 1 answer is written through the typed path, observed arriving in the browser through the change stream, and an attempted unauthorised stage advance is refused with no attestation changed.
title: A Stage 1 exchange reaches the browser and cannot cross the gate

statement: Stopping the supervisor leaves no child process, no bound port and no temporary file from that invocation; rerunning resumes the recorded session and the current stage, and the setup phase changes no bytes.
title: Shutdown is clean and a rerun resumes rather than restarting

statement: Each of the enumerated wrong states produces a refusal rather than an apparent success: wrong working directory, inspection denied, a configuration read attempted before consent, implicit adoption of a sole or default model, missing model authentication, an overbroad environment-only provider, a TTY-less login attempt, live-check denial and a malformed canary tool call, Tavily contacted before approval, a committed research choice with no local consent, trust denial, corrupt settings, untracked-state exposure, an interrupted transaction, an occupied port, an unrelated healthy HTTP service, tool signature drift, and a fake child returning plausible prose without Kiln tools.
title: Every negative control refuses

notes: ⚠️ NARROWED 2026-09-03. This previously required a REFUSAL with a stated recovery route, which is Kiln's behaviour and not Pi's, and could not have been evaluated when its task completed. It now records what Pi does; what Kiln must do about it is a separate criterion downstream of the setup command. ⚠️ 'STATED AS THE OBSERVED OUTCOME, NOT A REQUIRED ONE' is the load-bearing phrase: an observation that only passes when the runtime behaves the way the design hoped is not an observation.
statement: A manually invoked check records, against the pinned runtime alone: that the authentication-only step launches with exclusive terminal ownership; that a successful exit is distinguished from proven authentication by rediscovering auth afterwards rather than trusting the exit code; and what the same invocation does with no TTY, stated as the observed outcome — clean refusal, error, or indefinite wait — rather than as a required one. The transcript is retained. No claim is made here about Kiln's own refusal or its recovery messaging.
title: Pi's login step is observed owning the terminal, and its no-TTY behaviour is recorded

notes: ⚠️ THE SECOND HALF IS NOT OPTIONAL. A model appearing in `getAvailable()` after a login is consistent with the login having worked and equally consistent with it having been available already; only the revocation distinguishes them. ⚠️ THE 'FRESHLY CONSTRUCTED' CLAUSE MATTERS TOO: reusing a runtime built before the login would report a cached snapshot, and 'login UI exited' is not 'login succeeded' — the same rule section 6.2 applies to the exit code. ⚠️ FABRICATION IS EXCLUDED IN THE STATEMENT RATHER THAN IN A NOTE, because it is the cheap way to make this pass and it would prove a storage shape instead of usable authentication.
statement: A manual run against a real subscription records, with an isolated Pi configuration directory and a sanitized environment: that after Pi's interactive `/login` exits, a FRESHLY constructed `ModelRuntime` and `ModelRegistry` report the chosen built-in model in `getAvailable()` and return true from `hasConfiguredAuth()`; and that after the stored credential is removed or revoked, the same construction reports the model unavailable. The retained record is sanitized — asserted to contain no token, authorisation header, credential-derived value, username or absolute home path — and is labelled manual, account-bound and single-instance. A fabricated OAuth credential does not satisfy this criterion in any form.
title: OAuth is proved by a real login and its revocation, or it is not called verified

statement: Once the Kiln package exists, a real Pi run reports its capability signature in the loaded session, and a deliberate change to a measured tool signature causes a comparing consumer to refuse. Both halves are required: presence alone does not show that a consumer would notice its absence.
title: The capability signature is observed in a loaded session, and drift is detected

notes: ⚠️ THE PROCESS-NEVER-SPAWNED HALF IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. A refusal message printed just before launching the TUI anyway would satisfy a text assertion and still hang a CI job, which is the failure this exists to prevent — a hang is indistinguishable from work until a timeout. ⚠️ AND THE SECOND ROW IS A CONTROL: if the non-TTY path refused unconditionally, the refusal would prove nothing about TTY detection.
statement: With stdin not a TTY and no usable authentication already present, setup refuses BEFORE starting the interactive login step — verified by the login process never being spawned, not merely by the message printed — and prints both supported recovery routes: run setup from a local interactive terminal, or configure authentication on the target host outside Kiln and rerun with the required non-interactive decisions. With usable authentication already present, the same non-TTY invocation proceeds instead of refusing.
title: Setup refuses before launching login when there is no terminal, and names the way out

notes: PASS 2026-09-03, mechanised in `test/link-trace.test.mjs`. Each repair case asserts BOTH that the link is gone and that the lint finding it produced has cleared — `trace/wrong-target-type` for a wrong-type target, `trace/target-missing` for a deleted one, `lifecycle/trace-to-inactive` for a superseded one — because 'the array is shorter' was never the claim; 'the graph is repaired' is. Each fixture first asserts the finding EXISTS, so a case that stopped producing damage could not pass by repairing nothing. ⚠️ THE FIX IS AN ASYMMETRY AND BOTH HALVES ARE TESTED IN THE SAME FILE. Removal now inspects nothing about the target; addition still refuses a wrong type, a dangling reference and a malformed id. A later simplification that made them share one validation path would repair nothing and would pass a file that only tested removal. ⚠️ `answeredBy` OPENED FOR REMOVAL ONLY, and it is the only field that did. `supportedBy` and `refutedBy` still route to `unlinkEvidence` and `supersededBy` to `setLifecycle`, because those removal operations genuinely exist; `answeredBy` had none, which is what forced the deliberate exploitation of the companion defect during Phase 1. Adding an answer link still routes through `resolveQuestion`. ⚠️ THE WRITE DISCIPLINE IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the fresh-read-inside-the-lock is proved by editing the file between the artifact's creation and the unlink and requiring the edit to survive; the atomic write by requiring no temporary file beside the artifact; and the lock by requiring it released. #16's amend-on-change is covered, including that a no-op does not amend.
statement: `unlinkTrace` removes a link whose target is of the wrong type, whose target does not exist, and whose target has been superseded — each verified by the link being gone and the lint finding it clears. It removes `answeredBy` entries, which no operation could previously withdraw. It continues to refuse an unknown FIELD, and it preserves the lock, fresh-read and atomic-write discipline. Adding a link is unaffected and still validates the target type.
title: An invalid or stale link can be removed through the typed path

notes: PASS 2026-09-03. The guard is now `Array.isArray(effectiveSchema(schemas, type).properties[k]['x-traceTarget'])`, asked PER TYPE rather than as a union, because a name that is a link on one type need not be one on another. It is the same source `linkTrace` validates against, so the two cannot drift. ⚠️ THE COUNT WAS EIGHT, NOT NINE, AND MY EARLIER ACCOUNTS OF THIS DEFECT SAID NINE. They included `implementedBy`, which is deliberately NOT a trace field — the component schema says so explicitly: 'Paths rather than a trace field on purpose: code is not an artifact, and pretending it is would put the repository inside the planning model.' It declares no `x-traceTarget`, the derived guard leaves it alone, and a test asserts that it stays revisable. Enumerating from the schemas is what surfaced the miscount; a hand-written list would have carried it. ⚠️ THE SCHEMAS DECLARE 25 TRACE FIELDS AND THE OLD LIST HELD 17. Every name in the old list was a real trace field, so the defect was never a wrong entry — it was the eight that were never added, which is the failure mode of any guard maintained by hand beside a declaration that already exists. `reviseArtifact` already resolved the effective schema a few lines later, for materiality, under a comment reading 'never from a hardcoded field list'. The rule was in the file; it just had not been applied to the guard above it.
statement: `reviseArtifact` refuses every field the schemas declare with `x-traceTarget`, established by enumerating those fields from the schema set at test time and asserting a refusal for each — not by comparing against a second list written in the test. Adding a trace field to a schema therefore extends the guard with no code change, proved by introducing one in a copied schema set and requiring the refusal. The eight fields that were previously reachable — `acceptedBy`, `answeredBy`, `blocks`, `evaluates`, `fulfils`, `raisedBy`, `satisfies` and `verifies` — are refused, while a non-trace field on the same type stays revisable so the guard is discriminating rather than simply refusing everything.
title: The trace-field guard is derived from the schemas, and covers every declared trace field

statement: Every file the transaction may write is resolved through its deepest existing ancestor and proved to lie beneath a root the caller explicitly authorised, and the same proof is repeated under the lock immediately before each write. A junction or symbolic link on a target's path refuses and nothing is written through it, including a probe, even when the path spells as one inside the project. A root the caller did not pass is not a root the transaction can write to, and the transaction lock is not a writable target. Each target's plan key is derived from its resolved path, so two entries that reach the same physical file refuse whether they differ only in spelling or arrive through two authorised roots that overlap, and one file merged under any of its spellings reaches the single entry planned for it.
title: Every write target is identified by resolution, not by spelling

statement: The write plan is built while this process demonstrably holds the transaction lock, and planning refuses when it is not held. A plan that refuses leaves the project as it was found, directories included: every probe file and every directory created in order to probe is removed on every exit path. Where a removal cannot be completed, the transaction refuses and names each path it left behind, retaining alongside it whatever refusal caused the attempt — a cleanup failure is never reported as success. Absence is confirmed by observing the path, not by trusting the removal call's error code.
title: Planning holds the lock, and a refused plan leaves the project unchanged

statement: When the content a merge would produce is byte-identical to what is already on disk, the transaction performs no write. The evidence is the file's modification time, not the merge's reported status.
title: A merge that would produce the current bytes writes nothing

statement: The journal is a planned, contained target validated against its schema before each write, and it records the whole ordered phase plan up front, marking a phase running before that phase's work begins. On failure it survives, naming the last completed phase and an exact recovery command, and nothing already written is rolled back. On success it is deleted, and a deletion that fails for any reason other than the file already being absent is reported rather than swallowed.
title: The journal is a planned target whose lifecycle is never silent

statement: Given a transaction that already holds the project lock, the initializer runs inside it and produces content byte-identical to a standalone run, with the marked ignore block appended at most once and every pre-existing line intact; a second run inside a held transaction still reports already-initialised and does not touch the ignore file. The transaction is accepted only as an authenticated, currently live capability: an object carrying the right shape but not issued by the transaction module is refused, a genuine transaction whose run has finished is refused, and one holding a different project is refused — each without writing anything. Work runs inside a transaction only by being registered with it, so a collaborator authenticated at entry is also enrolled for its duration rather than left to run beside it. A transaction is revoked before its lock is released and every operation through a revoked transaction is refused. In-flight work is drained to quiescence before revocation, including work started by work already being drained, so nothing registered with the transaction is still running when the lock is released. Where any work was still running at the moment the body returned, that work completes under the lock and the run is reported failed. No claim is made about operations the body did not await which had already settled: they are indistinguishable from awaited ones and cannot cross the release boundary. An acquisition of a lock already held further up the same call stack is refused immediately rather than waiting out its bounded retry, that refusal expires with the lock so an acquisition from an async context descended from a released lock succeeds, and two concurrent independent acquisitions in one process still serialise.
title: The initializer runs inside an authenticated, live transaction

statement: Started with a run identifier and a project identifier, the launcher validates both before use and the application it starts answers its health endpoint with exactly those values — observed from the application's response, not from the launcher's own output, since a launcher printing an identifier proves only that it parsed one. The port is parsed rather than coerced, and a value that is not a whole number between 1 and 65535 is refused before anything is installed or built; an empty value is refused rather than treated as unset, because a supervisor whose port computation produced nothing would otherwise bind the default and then poll the port it believed it had chosen. A partial, malformed or present-but-empty identity is refused with the offending variable named and its value not echoed, never treated as a standalone run: standalone means the variables are absent, not blank, and starting anyway would produce a shell the supervisor can never recognise, reported to the operator as a readiness timeout two processes away from its cause. The launcher stops on the stop control message arriving on the stdin it was given, and stops equally on that stdin being closed with no message — a supervisor that dies cannot send anything, but the operating system closes its pipes regardless. Both paths terminate the child, remove the run directory, and free the port. The application is given no stdin at all, so it cannot read from the handle the launcher's own control channel arrives on. Interactive standalone operation — a terminal on stdin, no identity supplied — is unchanged, and the existing content-root refusal, single-child ownership and cleanup behaviour continue to hold. Standalone operation on a PIPED stdin is deliberately not unchanged: closing that pipe stops the launcher whether or not a supervisor is present, which is the intended behaviour rather than a preserved one. This criterion makes no claim about readiness: the launcher propagates an identity, and confirming that the process answering is the one this invocation started is the supervisor's to establish.
title: The launcher propagates a validated identity and stops through the stdin it is given

statement: When Pi exits, the supervisor sends the stop control message on the launcher's stdin, requests that stdin be ended, and then waits for the launcher to exit within a bounded period, escalating if it does not. Three facts are recorded separately: that the message was sent, that the end was requested, and whether the exit was actually observed. A run whose launcher was never seen to exit is reported as a failure with the address something may still be listening on — not as a success carrying the agent's own exit code, since the agent finishing cleanly says nothing about whether the launcher went. Writing to the pipe never throws: a stream error is delivered asynchronously, so it is listened for rather than wrapped in a try. An error observed before the shutdown result is finalised is recorded on that result; one arriving after it is not, and the criterion claims no more than that — what proves the launcher went is the observed exit, not the error record. That the launcher REACTS to a stop message and to a close is established elsewhere and is not what this asks; what this asks is that the supervisor performs the contract, since a supervisor that never sends anything is indistinguishable from one that does whenever the launcher would have exited for its own reasons. The wait is bounded in both directions: returning before the child is gone leaves a process holding the port, and waiting without limit replaces a hung application with a hung terminal. ⚠️ SIGNAL HANDLING, BOTH PROCESS TREES, GRACE PERIODS ACROSS PLATFORMS AND INVOCATION-OWNED FILE CLEANUP ARE NOT THIS CRITERION'S. They are ACC-0081's, on TSK-0058; claiming them here would mark work accepted that nothing has built.
title: The supervisor performs the Pi-exit handoff and observes the launcher go
